tools.name: mcp__visualize__show_widget
tools.description:
Show visual content — SVG graphics, diagrams, charts, or interactive HTML widgets — that renders inline alongside your text response.
Use for flowcharts, architecture diagrams, dashboards, forms, calculators, data tables, games, illustrations, or any visual content.
The code is auto-detected: starts with <svg = SVG mode, otherwise HTML mode.
A global sendPrompt(text) function is available — it sends a message to chat as if the user typed it.
IMPORTANT: Call read_me before your first show_widget call. Do NOT narrate or mention the read_me call to the user — call it silently, then respond as if you went straight to building the visualization.

loading_messages.description: 1–4 loading messages shown to the user while the visual renders, each roughly 5 words long. Write them in the same language the user is using. Use 1 for simple visuals, more for complex ones. If the topic is serious — illness, disease, pandemics, death, grief, war, conflict, poverty, disaster, trauma, abuse, addiction, medical decisions, politically charged subjects, or anything where the reader might be personally affected — keep these BORING: describe what the code is doing in the dullest generic way, no jargon-as-drama, no evocative terms. Pandemic growth model — NOT ['Simulating patient zero', 'Modeling the curve'] (documentary-narrator voice), YES ['Setting up the model', 'Running the calculation']. Cancer timeline — NOT ['Charting the battle ahead'], YES ['Laying out the stages']. If you have to ask whether it's serious, it is. Otherwise, have fun — reach for alliteration, puns, personification, wordplay, whatever lands in that language. Playful examples — revenue chart: ['Bribing bars to stand taller', 'Asking Q4 where it went']; kanban: ['Herding cards into columns', 'Dragging, dropping, not stopping'].

title.description: Short snake_case identifier for this visual. Must be specific and disambiguating — if the conversation has multiple visuals, this title alone should tell you which one is being referenced (e.g. 'q4_revenue_by_product_line' not 'chart', 'oauth_login_flow' not 'diagram'). Also used as the download filename, so no spaces or special characters.

widget_code.description: SVG or HTML code to render. For SVG: raw SVG code starting with <svg> tag, must use CSS variables for colors. Example: <svg viewBox="0 0 700 400" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg">...</svg>. For HTML: raw HTML content to render, do NOT include DOCTYPE, <html>, <head>, or <body> tags. Use CSS variables for theming. Keep background transparent and avoid top-level padding. Scripts are supported but execute after streaming completes.

tools.name: SubagentHandback
tools.description:
Deliver your final report to the agent that spawned you (your caller). Use it once, for that hand-off only: when your work is complete, call SubagentHandback({message: <your full report>}). The call ends your run, so do everything else first and put everything your caller needs in that one report. It is not a messaging channel: do not use it for progress updates or questions.

Only a report delivered through SubagentHandback reaches your caller; plain text you write at the end of your run is NOT delivered. There is no recipient parameter: the report can only go to your caller.

- claude-code-guide: Use this agent when the user asks questions ("Can Claude...", "Does Claude...", "How do I...") about: (1) Claude Code (the CLI tool) - features, hooks, slash commands, MCP servers, settings, IDE integrations, keyboard shortcuts; (2) Claude Agent SDK - building custom agents; (3) Claude API (formerly Anthropic API) - Messages API for directly passing messages to Claude, Tool Runner (`client.beta.messages.tool_runner`) for running an agentic loop over your own tools, manual tool-use loops, Managed Agents for server-hosted agents with a managed sandbox, prompt caching, and general Anthropic SDK usage; (4) Claude Tag (Claude in Slack) - what it is, setting it up for a Slack workspace, `/install-slack-app`; (5) `claude plugin eval` (writing and running plugin eval suites, its JSON/report, sandbox, CI) and the `/skill-doctor` report. **IMPORTANT:** Before spawning a new agent, check if there is already a running or recently completed claude-code-guide agent that you can continue via SendMessage. (Tools: Bash, Read, WebFetch, WebSearch)

1	import type { Block } from '../blocks/extract-blocks'
     2	import type { ReviewEdit, SuggestionOutput } from './schemas'
     3	
     4	export const MAX_REVIEW_EDITS = 6
     5	export const JUNK_MIN_ORIGINAL_WORDS = 15
     6	export const JUNK_MAX_REPLACEMENT_WORDS = 3
     7	
     8	const WORD = /[\p{L}\p{N}]+(?:['’-][\p{L}\p{N}]+)*/gu
     9	
    10	const wordCount = (text: string): number => text.match(WORD)?.length ?? 0
    11	
    12	export const isJunkReplacement = (
    13	  original: string,
    14	  replacement: string,
    15	): boolean =>
    16	  wordCount(original) > JUNK_MIN_ORIGINAL_WORDS &&
    17	  wordCount(replacement) < JUNK_MAX_REPLACEMENT_WORDS
    18	
    19	export type DropReason =
    20	  | 'unknown-block'
    21	  | 'code-block'
    22	  | 'occupied'
    23	  | 'duplicate-block'
    24	  | 'empty'
    25	  | 'unchanged'
    26	  | 'junk'
    27	  | 'over-limit'
    28	
    29	export type ValidatedEdit = ReviewEdit & { readonly block: Block }
    30	
    31	export type DroppedEdit = {
    32	  readonly edit: ReviewEdit
    33	  readonly reason: DropReason
    34	}
    35	
    36	export type ReviewValidationState = {
    37	  readonly validated: number
    38	  readonly seen: ReadonlySet<string>
    39	}
    40	
    41	export type ReviewValidationContext = {
    42	  readonly blocks: readonly Block[]
    43	  readonly occupied: ReadonlySet<string>
    44	}
    45	
    46	export type ReviewOutcome =
    47	  | { readonly type: 'validated'; readonly edit: ValidatedEdit }
    48	  | ({ readonly type: 'dropped' } & DroppedEdit)
    49	
    50	export const initialReviewState: ReviewValidationState = {
    51	  validated: 0,
    52	  seen: new Set(),
    53	}
    54	
    55	const dropReason = (
    56	  occupied: ReadonlySet<string>,
    57	  state: ReviewValidationState,
    58	  edit: ReviewEdit,
    59	  block: Block | undefined,
    60	): DropReason | undefined => {
    61	  if (block === undefined) return 'unknown-block'
    62	  if (block.kind === 'code') return 'code-block'
    63	  if (occupied.has(block.id)) return 'occupied'
    64	  if (state.seen.has(block.id)) return 'duplicate-block'
    65	  const replacement = edit.replacement.trim()
    66	  if (replacement === '') return 'empty'

import type { ClientError } from '../ai/errors'

export const describeError = (error: ClientError): string => {
  switch (error.type) {
    case 'out-of-credit':
      return 'OpenRouter is out of credit. Add credit to your OpenRouter account, then retry.'
    case 'rate-limited':
      return 'Too many requests. Wait a moment, then retry.'
    case 'timeout':
      return 'The model took too long to answer. Retry.'
    case 'network':
      return 'Could not reach the model. Check your connection, then retry.'
    case 'invalid-output':
      return 'The model returned an unusable answer twice. Retry, or rephrase the Instruction.'
    case 'aborted':
      return 'The request was cancelled.'
    case 'api':
      return `The model request failed (${error.status}): ${error.message}`
    case 'unknown':
      return `Something went wrong: ${error.message}`
  }
}

input.message:
Review of PR #12 (slice 5, Review pass). `pnpm test` passes (523 tests), `pnpm biome check` is clean and `pnpm build` is green. `__reviewDrops` does not appear in the prod bundle.

## Axis 1: Standards

1. **nit (taste)**, `src/ai/edits.ts:109-118`: `validateReviewEdits` uses `let state` and pushes into mutable arrays, which breaks the functional style in AGENTS.md. Fix: rewrite it as a `reduce` over `{ state, validated, dropped }`.
2. **nit (taste)**, `src/ai/dev-log.ts:37-44`: `appendReviewDrop` pushes into `target.__reviewDrops` in place. It matches the existing `appendAiCall`, so the inconsistency is acceptable. Fix: `target.__reviewDrops = [...(target.__reviewDrops ?? []), drop]`.
3. **nit**, `src/ai/edits.test.ts:177-210`: the junk guard is tested on both sides, but not at the exact boundaries (15 vs 16 original words, 2 vs 3 Replacement words). Fix: add two boundary cases.

GLOSSARY names (Review pass, Focus, Block, Suggestion, Replacement, Rationale, Accept, Reject) are used correctly. I found no `any`, no unnecessary comments, and no non-English code. Classes appear only through CodeMirror APIs. TDD covers mapping edits to Suggestions and `mapBlockRange` (multiple edits composed, before/inside/after the Block, deletion spanning a Block).

## Axis 2: Spec

1. **should-fix (real UX defect)**, `src/suggestions/state.ts:314-323` (`activeSuggestion`): when the cursor is in no Suggestion, Active falls back to the highest `sequence`. During a pass the card therefore jumps to each new arrival, and the last one is the least important, since edits arrive most important first. Fix: fall back to the newest non-review Suggestion, else the lowest-`sequence` review Suggestion, so the most important stays Active and new arrivals don't steal it. Add one test.
2. **should-fix (one line, worth doing now)**, `src/ai/errors.ts:37-45` (`fromApiCallError`): a stream that breaks after HTTP 200 with no `code` in the payload becomes `{type:'api', status:200}`. That renders as "The model request failed (200): Failed to process successful response". Fix: when the resolved status is 2xx, return a clearer type, e.g. `{ type: 'network', message }` or `unknown` with "The response stream broke". Add a test.
3. **should-fix (decide)**, `src/suggestions/review.ts:103-135` (`acceptAllPlan`): Accept all includes ready review Suggestions whose Refine is still working. It applies the pre-Refine Replacement, and `reconcile` then silently aborts the in-flight Refine. Single Accept does the same, so it is consistent, but with "all" the user may not notice. Fix: skip `refine.status === 'working'` in the plan (also in `openReviewCount`, so the button count matches), or document it as intended. A failed Refine keeps its last Replacement, which is fine.
4. **should-fix (verify in browser)**, `src/ui/App.tsx:46` (sticky header, `z-30`): CodeMirror tooltips (`.cm-tooltip`, z-index 500), which carry the suggestion cards and the ask bubble, will paint over the sticky header when you scroll. CM also won't hide them under it. Fix: pass `tooltips({ tooltipSpace: (view) => ({ ...view.dom.ownerDocument.documentElement.getBoundingClientRect(), top: headerBottom }) })`, or lower the tooltip z-index below the header.
5. **nit (risk is low)**, `src/ai/edits.ts:12-17` (junk guard): a Heading or list item over 15 words condensed to 1–2 words (e.g. "Getting started") is dropped as junk, though it can be a legitimate concision edit. Fix: exempt heading Blocks (`block.kind === 'heading'`), or apply the guard only to paragraphs.
6. **nit**, `src/ai/client.ts:~395` + `src/editor/review-runtime.ts:309`: the 6-edit cap and `firstSuggestionMs` both count at client validation, not at placement. If an edit is dropped at placement (`text-changed`/`occupied`), it still uses up a slot, and the recorded "time to first Suggestion" may refer to a Suggestion that never appeared. Fix: accept the gap and say so in the verification doc, or report the first placement time from the runtime.
7. **nit**, `src/editor/review-runtime.ts:346`: the toast's Retry closure holds the view. If it is clicked after unmount (12 s window), it dispatches to a destroyed view. Fix: clear the toast on unmount (`onReviewControls(null)` path), or guard `start` with a `destroyed` flag set in the ViewPlugin `destroy`.

Checked and correct:
- **Edits during the stream:** composed `ChangeDesc` per pass, reset on `startReviewEffect`, released on `endReviewEffect`. Edits before, inside, after and spanning a Block are handled. Undo/redo is safe: an insert then undo composes to no change, and the `doc.slice === block.text` check backs it up.
- **Accept all:** one transaction with `isolateHistory`; one undo restores the text. Ranges can't overlap; adjacent ranges are fine. Non-review Suggestions stay and are remapped; this is tested.
- **Stop / unmount:** Stop aborts and keeps the shown Suggestions. Late events are ignored through the `aborted` check and `run === null`. Unmount aborts through the ViewPlugin `destroy`, and no "reviewing" state is left after error, abort or unmount.
- **`done.error`:** the field is optional and additive. `scripts/bakeoff.ts` and the slice 2 tests still pass.
- **React ↔ CodeMirror bridge:** status is emitted only on change. Handlers sit in a ref, the pointerdown listener is cleaned up, and there is no re-render loop.
- **Spec points:** no Focus → default criteria; code and occupied Blocks are skipped.

All acceptance criteria are covered by tests or the verification doc.
